_readme: Claims about jurisdictions outside Italy. These sit in a separate file from facts.json for two reasons. First, facts.json is keyed by the bare figure and feeds GEO scoring, and several of these claims turn on numbers that mean something else elsewhere in this corpus: 10% is a Croatian transfer tax here and Italian new-build VAT on twenty other pages, 3% is a Portuguese IMT band here and an agency commission almost everywhere else. Registering them there would hand unrelated Italian pages a provenance they have not earned. Second, and the actual point: nobody on this project monitors the Portuguese State Budget, the Greek golden-visa thresholds, the Spanish autonomous communities or Maltese residence programmes the way Italian sources get checked. These figures will go out of date without anyone noticing. Each carries a reviewBy date; `npm run facts:review` fails once one is overdue, which is the whole mechanism. Reviewing means re-reading the primary source and either moving asOf and reviewBy forward or correcting every file listed.
_history: This site has already been bitten once by exactly this: the corpus carried a Greek golden-visa threshold of EUR 250,000 across several comparison pages long after Greece had moved to a two-tier EUR 400,000 / EUR 800,000 regime, and it was caught by hand in the August 2026 audit rather than by any check. That figure had no watcher. This file is the watcher.

claims.claim: Greece runs a tiered residence-by-investment property threshold of EUR 400,000 in most of the country and EUR 800,000 in the highest-demand zones, replacing the former flat EUR 250,000
claims.source: Greek Law 5100/2024 amending the residence permit investment thresholds

claims.claim: Portugal no longer grants residence by investment through residential property purchase; the property routes were removed from the programme
claims.source: Portugal Mais Habitacao, Law 56/2023

claims.claim: Spain has ended its residence-by-property-investment route, so the former EUR 500,000 threshold no longer buys residence
claims.source: Spanish Organic Law 1/2025 repealing the investor residence provisions of Law 14/2013

claims.claim: Croatia charges a 3% real estate transfer tax on resale purchases, with new builds from a VAT-registered seller falling under VAT instead
claims.source: Croatian Real Estate Transfer Tax Act

claims.claim: Malta's residence routes run on programme-specific property value and contribution floors rather than on a single purchase threshold, and the citizenship route was struck down by the Court of Justice of the European Union in 2025
claims.source: Malta Permanent Residence Programme regulations; CJEU judgment in Commission v Malta (C-181/23)

claims.claim: French frais de notaire on an existing property run to roughly 7-8% of price, the great majority of which is transfer duty rather than the notaire's own fee
claims.source: Conseil superieur du notariat published fee scales

claims.claim: The EU Entry/Exit System reaches full operation across external borders on 10 April 2026, with ETIAS following in 2027, which is what governs how long a non-EU owner may stay at an Italian property
claims.source: Regulation (EU) 2017/2226 and the Commission progressive rollout timetable

claims.claim: EPBD IV sets stock-average residential energy reductions of 16% by 2030 and 20-22% by 2035 and does NOT impose a minimum energy class on an individual home; member states had until 29 May 2026 to transpose it
claims.source: Directive (EU) 2024/1275 arts. 9 and 35

claims.claim: Spain's wealth tax carries a state exemption of €700,000 of net wealth per person, applying to non-residents on Spanish assets, with a further allowance of up to €300,000 against a main residence available to residents only; the state scale runs progressively from 0.2% to 3.5% and autonomous communities modify the outcome; on a sale by a non-resident the buyer withholds 3% of the price on account of the seller's capital gains tax
claims.source: Ley 19/1991 del Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio, state scale and minimo exento; autonomous community variations

claims.claim: Croatia charges real estate transfer tax at 3% of market value rather than of the stated contract price; a new build sold by a VAT-registered developer carries 25% VAT instead and no transfer tax; from contracts or occupancy from 1 January 2025 first-time buyers may obtain a full refund of transfer tax and up to half of the VAT, within size and price limits
claims.source: Croatian Real Estate Transfer Tax Act as administered by Porezna uprava; 2025 first-time buyer relief

claims.claim: Unoccupied dwellings run at roughly 7.8% in France and 4.4% in Germany, far below Italy's share of about 27.2%
claims.source: National statistical comparisons of unoccupied dwellings, reported alongside ISTAT figures for Italy

claims.claim: Law 74/2025, in force from 28 March 2025, limits automatic recognition of Italian citizenship by descent to applicants with an Italian-born parent or grandparent, ending the previously unlimited bloodline for great-grandparents and beyond from 27 March 2025
claims.source: Legge 74/2025 (conversion of DL 36/2025, the Tajani decree); cross-checked against boccadutri.com and myitalianfamily.com summaries, September 2026

claims.claim: The Italian Constitutional Court heard the challenges to the Law 74/2025 descent restrictions on 11 March 2026 and announced on 12 March 2026 that it dismissed the questions of constitutional legitimacy, confirming the generational limit stands
claims.source: Corte Costituzionale ruling announced 12 March 2026; reported by boccadutri.com and cross-checked in independent search results, September 2026

claims.claim: Naturalisation by residence is reduced to 2 years for applicants with an Italian-born parent or grandparent who do not meet the descent conditions, against the ordinary 10 years for other non-EU nationals
claims.source: Legge 74/2025 residency provisions; cross-checked against boccadutri.com summary of the 2026 rules, September 2026

claims.claim: Declaration deadlines for minor children under Law 74/2025: children born before 25 May 2025 have until 31 May 2029, and children born after that date have 3 years from birth
claims.source: Legge 74/2025 transitional provisions for minors; cross-checked against boccadutri.com, September 2026

claims.claim: Italy suspended its Investor Visa for Russian and Belarusian nationals in July 2023, acting on European Commission Recommendation C(2022)554. The bar extends to dual nationals holding either passport, so a second citizenship does not reopen the route.
claims.source: Ministry of Enterprise investor visa portal (investorvisa.mise.gov.it) suspension notice; European Commission Recommendation C(2022)554 of 28 March 2022

claims.claim: Before the suspension, Italy had issued investor visas to at least 32 Russian citizens from 36 applications, more than the 12 issued to United States applicants and the 12 issued to United Kingdom applicants combined.
claims.source: Italian Ministry of Enterprise application data as reported when the suspension was announced, August 2023

claims.claim: The investor residence permit is issued for two years and renews in three-year increments, each renewal conditional on the qualifying investment still being in place. Nulla osta review runs about 25 to 35 days and the qualifying transfer must complete within three months of entry.
claims.source: Ministry of Enterprise investor visa policy guidance; consistent with the programme portal

claims.claim: Italy's digital nomad and remote worker route was created by an inter-ministerial decree of 29 February 2024, in force from 5 April 2024, with operational detail set by a later implementing decree signed by the Ministers of the Interior, Labour and Foreign Affairs, and was folded into the Immigration Code in 2026. It sits outside the decreto flussi quota and needs no employment clearance.
claims.source: Inter-ministerial decree 29 February 2024; Italian consular visa pages, checked 6 September 2026

claims.claim: The income floor is three times the annual healthcare exemption threshold, about EUR 24,790 a year or EUR 2,066 a month. Consular practice sits above it, commonly EUR 25,500 to EUR 28,000, while the New York consulate has continued to reference EUR 24,789.
claims.source: Italian consular visa pages, London and New York, checked 6 September 2026; the statutory basis is the healthcare exemption multiple

claims.claim: Consulates implement the same decree differently: the Italian Consulate General in London publishes the route as being for self-employed applicants only, while New York publishes it as a combined digital nomad and remote worker visa.
claims.source: Published visa pages of the Italian Consulates General in London and New York, checked 6 September 2026

claims.claim: IRPEF bands for 2026 are 23% up to EUR 28,000, 33% from EUR 28,001 to EUR 50,000 and 43% above EUR 50,000. The middle band was cut from 35% to 33% by the 2026 budget law, the reduction applies only up to EUR 200,000 of income, and the maximum annual saving is about EUR 440.
claims.source: Legge di Bilancio 2026, Legge 30 dicembre 2025 n. 199

claims.claim: Foreign pensioners transferring tax residence to a qualifying comune in Abruzzo, Molise, Campania, Puglia, Basilicata, Calabria, Sicily or Sardinia may elect a 7% substitute tax on ALL foreign-source income, for the year of transfer and the nine following, ten tax periods in all. They must not have been Italian tax resident in any of the five preceding years. Article 26 of Law 11 March 2026 no. 34 amended Article 24-ter TUIR to raise the population ceiling from 20,000 to 30,000 residents, in force 7 April 2026, bringing roughly 74 further comuni into scope.
claims.source: Article 24-ter TUIR as amended by Article 26 of Legge 11 marzo 2026 n. 34 (Legge annuale PMI), published in Gazzetta Ufficiale 23 March 2026, in force 7 April 2026

claims.claim: Voluntary SSN registration for a non-EU retiree costs between EUR 2,000 and about EUR 2,788.87 a year, scaled to income, paid on form F24. The contribution is tied to the calendar year and expires on 31 December whatever month it was paid, so registering late in a year means paying again in January.
claims.source: Italian SSN voluntary registration rules for non-EU residents, contribution schedule current at September 2026

claims.claim: The elective residence visa income test is EUR 31,160 a year for the main applicant, plus 20% for a dependent spouse and 5% per dependent child, putting a couple near EUR 38,000. In July 2025 the administrative court in Rome overturned a refusal in which a consulate had applied the threshold per person rather than to the household.
claims.source: Italian consular guidance on the elective residence visa; July 2025 administrative court ruling reported on the per-person application of the threshold

claims.claim: A bilateral Italy-UK agreement on mutual recognition of driving licences has been in force since 30 March 2023 and is valid until 30 March 2028. A UK licence may be exchanged for an Italian one without theory or practical test where the holder has been resident in Italy for less than six years at the time of application; those resident by 31 December 2020 are exempt from the six-year limit.
claims.source: Italy-UK agreement on mutual recognition of driving licences, in force 30 March 2023 (UK treaty series CS UK Italy 1.2023)

claims.claim: A UK national at State Pension age can claim an S1 form before leaving the UK, which gives access to the Italian national health service with the cost met by the UK government. Those below State Pension age register with the SSN voluntarily and pay the contribution themselves, or hold private cover.
claims.source: UK-EU social security coordination under the Withdrawal Agreement and the Trade and Cooperation Agreement; Italian SSN registration rules

claims.claim: The UK State Pension is not frozen in Italy and continues to uprate annually. Protection derives from the Withdrawal Agreement for those resident before 31 December 2020 and from the Trade and Cooperation Agreement for later arrivals.
claims.source: UK-EU Withdrawal Agreement and Trade and Cooperation Agreement, social security coordination provisions

claims.claim: Personal property imported when transferring normal residence from a third country into the EU is admitted free of import duty and VAT, provided the person had normal residence outside the EU for at least twelve consecutive months, the goods were owned and used for at least six months before shipment, they arrive within twelve months of establishing the new residence, and they are not sold, lent, pledged or rented for twelve months after clearance without notifying customs.
claims.source: Council Regulation (EC) No 1186/2009, Title II, reliefs on transfer of normal residence

claims.claim: A buyer of an Italian condominium unit is jointly liable with the seller for contributions relating to the current management year and the preceding one, with no distinction between ordinary and extraordinary charges. The year is the management year of 365 days set by the assembly or the regolamento, not the calendar year. The seller remains jointly bound until the transfer is notified to the administrator.
claims.source: Article 63, fourth paragraph, of the provisions implementing the Italian Civil Code (disposizioni di attuazione del codice civile)

claims.claim: An administrator may obtain an immediately enforceable payment order (decreto ingiuntivo immediatamente esecutivo) for unpaid contributions without assembly authorisation, and may suspend a defaulting owner from shared services capable of separate enjoyment once arrears exceed six months. Under article 1129 the administrator must begin recovery within six months of the close of the financial year in which the debt arose unless the assembly exempts them.
claims.source: Article 63 and article 1129 of the Italian Civil Code and its implementing provisions

claims.claim: Stairs and lifts are maintained and replaced at 50% in proportion to the value of each unit and 50% in proportion to each floor's height above ground, so upper floors carry more of a lift replacement than lower floors of the same size.
claims.source: Article 1124 of the Italian Civil Code
